correctness.rationale: The gram sectors follow from exact character orthogonality and the conditional first and second weight moments. Positivity follows because the radius-one ball contains all one-coordinate perturbations and the radial variance is positive. The subcritical deficit is geometrically dominated in two moments, giving exact asymptotics of both extreme eigenvalues and the \(n^{3/2}\) coefficient. Standardized conditional binomial moments converge in the Gaussian window via bounded fourth moments; above the mean the omitted binomial tail makes the Gram approach identity. The packaged verify.py independently diagonalizes 36 actual finite Fourier matrices and numerically checks representative limits. No finite experiment is substituted for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A sharp singular-condition-number threshold for deterministic sampling from all low-weight q-ary words determines worst-case reconstruction stability rather than merely algebraic rank. It locates an \(n^{3/2}\) loss with exact density-dependent constant, a universal truncated-Gaussian crossover, and asymptotic isometry above the typical weight; these distinctions matter to sampling-density design. The finite shell algebra itself is acknowledged as prior-covered, and the scientific value rests on the full quantitative three-regime result.
